title: 1956 Grand Canyon mid-air collision
summary: A TWA Constellation and United DC-7 collided over the Grand Canyon at 10:32 am in uncontrolled airspace. The two aircraft collided at an angle of about 25 degrees, and the DC-7's left wing clipped the Constellation's vertical stabilizer and fuselage, causing the tail assembly to break away. The Constellation entered a near-vertical terminal velocity dive and disintegrated on impact, while the DC-7 entered a rapidly descending left spiral and crashed into a cliff. All 128 people aboard both aircraft were killed.
probable_cause: The collision took place in uncontrolled airspace where it was the pilots' responsibility to maintain separation by 'see and be seen'. Investigation could not determine conclusively how much opportunity was available for the pilots to see and avoid each other due to uncertainty regarding high altitude visibility.

The collision highlighted the antiquated state of air traffic control.

title: 1960 New York air disaster
summary: On December 16, 1960, United Air Lines Flight 826, a Douglas DC-8 heading for Idlewild Airport, collided in midair with Trans World Airlines Flight 266, a Lockheed L-1049 Super Constellation descending toward LaGuardia Airport. The Constellation crashed on Miller Field in Staten Island and the DC-8 in Park Slope, Brooklyn, killing all 128 aboard the two aircraft and six people on the ground. The accident was the world's deadliest aviation disaster at the time and remains the deadliest accident in United Airlines history.
probable_cause: United 826 had only one operational VOR receiver after the other became inoperative, which presented difficulty for the pilots to identify the PRESTON intersection. ATC was not informed of the inoperative receiver. The aircraft was estimated to be traveling at 301 knots when it collided, several miles beyond the PRESTON clearance limit.

title: Flying Tiger Line 739
summary: Flying Tiger Line Flight 739, a Lockheed Super Constellation chartered by the US Army, disappeared on 16 March 1962 while en route from Guam to the Philippines with 107 military personnel and crew aboard. A civilian tanker observed what appeared to be an in-flight explosion. The Civil Aeronautics Board determined Flight 739 probably exploded in-flight based on tanker observations.

title: Air France 007
summary: Air France Flight 007, a Boeing 707 taking off from Orly on 3 June 1962, lifted off but the main landing gear remained on the ground. The crew attempted to abort the takeoff, using wheel brakes and reverse thrust to stop the aircraft. The aircraft skidded off the runway and struck the town of Villeneuve-le-Roi. Investigation indicated the elevator trim motor may have failed.

title: Trans-Canada Air Lines 831
summary: Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 831, a Douglas DC-8 departing Montreal on 29 November 1963 in poor weather, deviated from expected flight path about five minutes after takeoff and began a quick descent. At 6:33 p.m., the jet struck the ground at an estimated 470 mph while descending at approximately 55 degrees. The investigation could not determine the exact cause but pointed to problems in the jet's pitch trim system.
probable_cause: The investigation could not determine the exact cause of the accident, though problems in the aircraft's pitch trim system were identified as a possible factor.

title: Air India 101
summary: Air India Flight 101, a Boeing 707 named Kanchenjunga, crashed into Mont Blanc in France on 24 January 1966 while on approach to Geneva. The pilot, thinking he had passed Mont Blanc, started to descend and flew into the Mont Blanc massif at 4750 meters elevation. All 117 people aboard were killed.
probable_cause: The pilot believed the aircraft had passed Mont Blanc when instructed to descend for Geneva, but the aircraft had not yet cleared the mountain. The crew had one VOR receiver unserviceable and failed to confirm their position before descending.

title: BOAC 911
summary: BOAC Flight 911, a Boeing 707 departing Tokyo Haneda for Hong Kong, encountered severe clear-air turbulence over Mount Fuji and disintegrated in mid-air on 5 March 1966. The structural failure began with the vertical stabilizer attachment failing under extreme aerodynamic loads. All 124 occupants were killed.
probable_cause: The aircraft encountered abnormally severe clear-air turbulence over Gotemba City which imposed gust loads considerably in excess of the aircraft's structural design, causing the vertical stabilizer to fail and leading to airframe breakup in flight.

factors.evidence: the vertical stabiliser attachment to the fuselage failed first

events.text: The aircraft began taxiing at 13:50 and took off into the northwest wind at 13:58.
After takeoff, the aircraft made a continuous climbing right turn over Tokyo Bay and rolled out on a southwest heading.
At an altitude of approximately 16000 ft, well above the 12388 ft mountain peak, the aircraft encountered strong turbulence.
The vertical stabiliser attachment to the fuselage failed first, and the ventral fin and all four engine pylons failed due to leftward over-stress.
The aircraft entered a flat spin, with the forward fuselage section and the outer starboard wing breaking off shortly before impact.
Flight 911 left a debris field 16 km long after impact with the ground.

title: South African Airways 228
summary: South African Airways Flight 228, a new Boeing 707 taking off from Windhoek on 20 April 1968 in a dark, moonless night with no ground lights, initially climbed to 650 ft then leveled off and started to descend. Fifty seconds after takeoff the aircraft flew into terrain at approximately 271 knots. The crew failed to maintain safe airspeed and altitude by not observing flight instruments.
probable_cause: The captain and first officer failed to maintain a safe airspeed and altitude and a positive climb by not observing flight instruments during takeoff. Loss of situational awareness in dark, moonless night conditions contributed; the crew misread altitude and vertical speed indicators.

Fifty seconds after take-off, the aircraft flew into the ground in flight configuration at approximately 271 knots.

title: Air France 1611
summary: Air France Flight 1611, a Sud Aviation Caravelle, took off from Ajaccio at 10:09 on 11 September 1968, bound for Nice. The flight was initially without incident and weather conditions were sunny. At 10:30 local time, on descending between flight level 90 to flight level 70, the flight crew declared an emergency mentioning a fire on board. The radio and radar contact was lost after a final contact at 10:33, and a kerosene slick and floating debris were discovered, confirming that the plane had crashed into the sea with all 95 people aboard.
probable_cause: The report surmised that the loss of the aircraft was caused by a fire in the passenger toilet caused either by a defective water heater or a cigarette discarded in a waste bin. The direct cause of loss of control could not be definitively established: it may be related to the pilots' physical incapacity caused either by toxic gas emissions or by passengers invading the cockpit.

title: 1969 Yukhnov mid-air collision
summary: On 23 June 1969, an Ilyushin Il-14M operating as Aeroflot Flight 831 collided in mid-air with an Antonov An-12BP of the Soviet Air Force over Yukhnovsky District. The Il-14 disobeyed ATC instructions and climbed to 3000 m to avoid turbulence, where the An-12 formation was flying. All 120 occupants of both aircraft perished.
probable_cause: The pilots of the Il-14 disobeyed instructions from air traffic control and climbed to the altitude of 3000 m to avoid turbulence and clouds, where the formation of An-12s were flying. The An-12 pilots also flew slightly lower than their assigned altitude of 3000 m, contributing to the collision.

events.text: At 13:25 the An-12 involved in the accident took off from Kedainiai Air Base as the last one in a formation of four.

At 14:40:55 the crew of Il-14 contacted air traffic control and requested permission to climb to 3300 m due to severe turbulence and cumulus clouds.
Due to the An-12s at 3000 m, the controller instead offered permission to descend to 2700 m, but the pilots of the Il-14 declined.

The An-12 lost the right wing and right wing engines from the impact, causing it to spin to the ground, while the Il-14 lost part of the right wing and the upper part of the fuselage.

title: Air Canada 621
summary: Air Canada Flight 621, a Douglas DC-8 landing at Toronto on 5 July 1970, touched down hard which ruptured the right fuel tanks. The investigation attributed the accident to pilot error and non-compliance with spoiler deployment procedures, where the first officer deployed spoilers during the flare instead of arming them.
probable_cause: The crew deviated from approved spoiler procedures; the first officer deployed spoilers during the flare instead of arming them, causing the aircraft to sink heavily and resulting in a hard landing that ruptured fuel tanks which subsequently exploded.

title: Aviogenex 130
summary: Aviogenex Flight 130, an international charter from Gatwick to Rijeka, took off at 16:33 GMT and suffered structural failure during landing on 23 May 1971. The Tupolev Tu-134A flipped over and caught fire. Investigation found that the crew might have suffered an optical illusion due to heavy showers and dusk that could have led them to believe the runway was closer and lower than it actually was. The crew executed an overly steep and fast descent in the last phase of final approach, causing a hard touchdown and breakage of the right wing, killing 78 out of 83 people.
probable_cause: Optical illusion caused by dusk, rain and water on runway led the crew to believe they were closer and higher from the runway than actually the case. The crew made a sharp nose-down input and reduced power to idle in the final phase, causing the aircraft to reach excessive speed and contact the runway with forces that broke the right wing.

title: All Nippon Airways 58
summary: On 30 July 1971, a Japan Air Self-Defense Force F-86F Sabre jet fighter collided with All Nippon Airways Flight 58, a Boeing 727 airliner climbing to its cruising altitude of about 28000 ft. The trainee Sabre pilot was told by his instructor to break away from Flight 58, but was already too late. The leading edge of the Sabre's right wing struck the Boeing's left tailplane at an altitude of 26000 ft. The damage caused the Boeing to go out of control; it entered a steep dive and disintegrated in mid-air, killing all 162 people aboard the airliner.
probable_cause: A trainee pilot in a JASDF F-86F Sabre, unaware of the ANA aircraft, collided with the Boeing 727. Although told by his instructor to break away, the trainee pilot's avoidance was too late. The Sabre's right wing struck the Boeing's left tailplane, causing fatal structural damage.

title: Eastern Air Lines 401
summary: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 crashed in the Florida Everglades shortly before midnight after the autopilot inadvertently disconnected. A subtle bump of the yoke switched the autopilot from altitude hold to Control Wheel Steering mode. While the crew was focused on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light, they did not notice the autopilot disconnection and the aircraft gradually lost altitude until striking the ground.

title: Kano air disaster
summary: A Boeing 707 crashed at Kano International Airport while attempting to land in high winds. The aircraft landed nose wheel first and the nose wheel collapsed after hitting a depression in the runway. The right main landing gear subsequently collapsed, the aircraft turned 180 degrees, left the runway and burst into flames. All 176 fatalities were a result of the fire.

title: Agadir air disaster
summary: A Royal Air Maroc Boeing 707 flight from Paris to Agadir crashed into a mountain on August 3, 1975 while descending to land at Inezgane Airport. The aircraft was flying over the Atlas Mountains in heavy fog. The right wingtip and number 4 engine struck a peak about 45 miles northeast of Agadir at 2400 feet altitude. The aircraft lost control and crashed into a valley. All 188 passengers and crew aboard were killed, making it the deadliest crash involving a Boeing 707.
probable_cause: The cause of the crash was determined to be pilot error in not ensuring positive course guidance before beginning descent. The aircraft had not followed the usual north-south corridor generally used for flights to Agadir and was flying from the northeast over the Atlas Mountains.

title: Turkish Airlines 452
summary: Turkish Airlines Flight 452 crashed into Karatepe Hill near Isparta after the first officer mistook city lights of Isparta for the runway at Antalya. The pilots attempted visual flight at night instead of using instruments, mistaking dark mountains for the Mediterranean Sea. The aircraft descended too early and crashed into a hill.

title: Malaysian Airline System 653
summary: Malaysian Airline System Flight 653 was hijacked as it descended toward Kuala Lumpur on 4 December 1977. Someone knocked on the cockpit door and one or more hijackers suddenly barged into the cockpit. The pilots were forced to cut off all communications. Investigators heard a series of gunshots on the cockpit voice recorder and concluded that both pilots were fatally shot, leaving the aircraft professionally uncontrolled until it impacted the ground at near-vertical angle at Tanjung Kupang, killing all 100 people aboard.

title: Icelandic Airlines 001
summary: Loftleiðir Flight 001 crashed on approach to Colombo on November 15, 1978. The crew was cleared to descend on runway 22 for an ILS approach. The aircraft descended dangerously towards the ground and crashed into a rubber and coconut plantation. The crash killed 183 out of 262 passengers and crew.

title: Pan Am 759
summary: Pan Am Flight 759 crashed in Kenner, Louisiana, minutes after takeoff when the Boeing 727 encountered a microburst that produced a downdraft and decreasing headwind. The aircraft lifted off and climbed briefly then began to descend, striking trees. Eight people on the ground were killed. The NTSB determined the probable cause was microburst-induced wind shear during liftoff.
probable_cause: The aircraft's encounter with microburst-induced wind shear during liftoff, which imposed a downdraft and a decreasing headwind. Contributing factors included the limited capability of then-current wind shear detection technology.

title: Independent Air 1851
summary: Independent Air Flight 1851 struck Pico Alto mountain on approach to Santa Maria Airport in the Azores on February 8, 1989. During descent, the trainee air traffic controller transmitted an incorrect QNH that was 9 hPa too high. The crew misheard due to non-standard phraseology and used the wrong altimeter setting. The aircraft descended below safe altitude and struck the mountain, killing all 144 aboard.
probable_cause: During the transmission, the trainee controller transmitted an incorrect QNH that was 9 hPa too high and used non-standard terminology. The crew did not fully hear the approach instructions and misheard the pressure setting, leading them to descend below safe altitude. The crew's failure to question the high pressure reading contributed to the accident.

factors.evidence: The trainee controller transmitted an incorrect QNH that was 9 hPa too high and used non-standard terminology at one point saying 'one octant' instead of decimal.
The crew misheard and falsely determined there were no clouds below 2,000 feet based on incorrect altitude readings.
The aircraft descended below safe altitude when they declared cleared to two thousand feet instead of the transmitted 3,000 feet.
The aircraft struck Pico Alto mountain while on approach to Santa Maria Airport.

events.text: Flight 1851 departed Bergamo Airport with communication difficulties on high frequencies
Crew contacted Santa Maria Air Traffic Control center and was handled by a trainee controller
Controller transmitted an incorrect QNH of 1027 hPa when it was actually 1018.7 hPa
The crew told the controller they were cleared to two thousand feet instead of the transmitted three thousand feet
The aircraft struck Pico Alto mountain and was destroyed with all 144 on board killed

title: Avianca 052
summary: Avianca Flight 052 ran out of fuel after three holding patterns and a failed landing attempt at JFK, crashing onto a hillside in Cove Neck on Long Island. Due to poor communication and inadequate fuel management, the flight became critically low on fuel but controllers did not recognize the emergency because pilots failed to use the word 'emergency'. The crew's failure to properly declare a fuel emergency and inadequate traffic flow management by the FAA contributed to the accident.
probable_cause: The flight crew failed to properly declare a fuel emergency and inadequately managed the fuel load. Poor communication between crew and controllers and lack of standardized terminology for emergency fuel states contributed.

factors.evidence: The Boeing 707 flying this route ran out of fuel after a failed attempt to land at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK).
First Officer Klotz radioed the controller, saying, 'ah well I think we need priority we're passing [unintelligible]'.
This dire situation was not recognized as an emergency by the controllers because of the failure of the pilots to use the word 'emergency'.
The flight was placed in three holding patterns.
The Boeing 707 flying this route crashed on a hillside in the small village of Cove Neck, New York.

events.text: Flight 052 entered its first holding pattern over Norfolk at 19:04.
The flight was placed in a second holding pattern from 19:43 to 20:12.
The flight entered its third holding pattern from 20:18 to 20:47.
At 21:24:06, the captain asked the first officer to tell them we are in an emergency.
The aircraft crashed on a hillside in the small village of Cove Neck, New York.

title: 1990 Guangzhou Baiyun airport collisions
summary: On 2 October 1990, a hijacked Boeing 737-200 operating Xiamen Airlines Flight 8301 collided with two other aircraft at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport while attempting to land. The hijacked aircraft struck parked China Southwest Airlines Flight 4305, a Boeing 707, first, then collided with CAAC Flight 3523, a Boeing 757 waiting to take off, flipping onto its back. A total of 128 people were killed, including seven of nine crew members and 75 of 93 passengers on Flight 8301 and 46 of 110 passengers on Flight 3523, making the incident the deadliest aircraft hijacking prior to the September 11 attacks.
probable_cause: The hijacking led to collision with parked aircraft. The hijacker demanded diversion to Taiwan, but the aircraft was directed to land at Baiyun Airport instead. Procedural failures in handling the hijacking were acknowledged by authorities.

factors.evidence: Jiang Xiaofeng displayed wires in his hand and claimed he was carrying 7 kilograms of explosives, demanding that the flight be diverted to Taiwan.
Authorities acknowledged procedural failures in handling the hijacking.
The hijacked aircraft collided with two other aircraft at the old Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport.
The hijacked aircraft struck parked China Southwest Airlines Flight 4305 first, a Boeing 707, then collided with CAAC Flight 3523, a Boeing 757 waiting to take off, flipping onto its back.

events.text: Jiang Xiaofeng left his seat, rushed toward the cockpit holding a black plastic box, forcefully pounded on the cockpit door and opened it, displaying wires and claiming to carry explosives.
Jiang ordered that everyone except the captain leave the cockpit, and cockpit audio was transmitted to the control tower via radio communication systems.
The Civil Aviation Administration's Central South Regional Bureau authorized the aircraft to land at any airport, and Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport was shut down.
The hijacked aircraft struck parked China Southwest Airlines Flight 4305 first, then collided with CAAC Flight 3523, a Boeing 757 waiting to take off.

title: PIA 268
summary: PIA Flight 268 descended below cleared altitude during approach and crashed into the 8,250 ft Mahabharat Range mountain at Bhattedanda. The aircraft initiated each descent step too early, descending 1,300 feet below cleared altitude by the Sierra reporting point. Investigators determined pilot error as the primary cause, with contributions from poor visibility, lack of radar surveillance, and unclear approach plates.
probable_cause: Pilot error: the aircraft initiated each step of descent one step too early, approaching the Mahabharat Range at insufficient altitude. The lack of radar prevented controllers from warning of inappropriate altitude.

factors.evidence: The aircraft initiated each step of its descent one step too early.
The aircraft approached the Mahabharat Range at an insufficient altitude and crashed into the south slope.
Visibility was poor due to overcast conditions.
The approach plates for Kathmandu issued to PIA pilots were also determined to be unclear.
The aircraft crashed at approximately 7300 ft into the side of the 8,250 ft mountain at Bhattedanda, disintegrating on impact.

events.text: The aircraft was cleared for an approach from the south called the Sierra approach.
The aircraft was to then descend in seven steps to 5,800 feet.
The aircraft initiated each step of its descent one step too early.
The aircraft crashed at approximately 7300 ft into the side of the 8,250 ft mountain at Bhattedanda.

title: Palair Macedonian Airlines 301
summary: The Fokker 100 crashed shortly after takeoff in snowy conditions due to ice accumulation on the wings. The aircraft had been parked in snow and refueled; ice around the wing roots melted from fuel temperature but ice on the wingtips remained. The crew elected not to de-ice the aircraft and encountered control problems during takeoff that caused the crash.
probable_cause: Ice accumulation on the aircraft wings that was inadequately de-iced before takeoff. The crew conducted only a tactile check and opted not to use ground de-icing equipment.

factors.evidence: During the refueling, the ice around the wings' roots had melted due to the temperature of the fuel, while the ice on the tips hadn't.
The crew opted not to de-ice the aircraft, thinking that most of the ice had melted and the remaining was safe enough for flying.
A crew switch was conducted and a new set of pilots were brought in; the Macedonian co-pilot was undergoing training to transfer from Boeing 737 to Fokker 100.
The FSE performed a tactile check by rubbing his hand over the wings but did not request de-icing.
The aircraft eventually encountered control problems during takeoff, which caused it to crash.

events.text: The aircraft arrived in Skopje after a flight from Frankfurt, and was parked in Skopje in snowy conditions.
The aircraft was refueled with approximately 2,000 liters of fuel during which ice around the wings' roots had melted due to the temperature of the fuel.
A second refueling was commenced and the FSE performed a tactile check by rubbing his hand over the wings, but did not request de-icing.
The aircraft was cleared for take-off and eventually encountered control problems during takeoff, which caused it to crash.

title: Khabarovsk United Air Group 3949
summary: Khabarovsk United Air Group Flight 3949 crashed on 7 December 1995 during automated flight at 10600 m, killing all ninety-eight people aboard. The aircraft had instantaneously banked to the left shortly after taking off due to mechanical failure. Following maintenance, the aircraft had a tendency to roll to the left without any command from the pilots, but this issue was not rectified. The crew were unaware that the aircraft had banked to the right. Without proper monitoring and lack of alarm, the aircraft entered a heavy turn to the right, spiralling down without any possible recovery.
probable_cause: The crash was caused by a combination of mechanical failure, pilot error and design flaw. An unresolved mechanical issue causing roll to the left led the crew to conduct fuel transfer as a corrective action. The crew were unaware the aircraft had banked to the right, and without adequate monitoring systems or warnings, the aircraft entered an unrecoverable spiral descent.

factors.evidence: The aircraft had instantaneously banked to the left shortly after taking off due to mechanical failure.
Following maintenance, the aircraft had a tendency to roll to the left without any command from the pilots, and the issue was not rectified.
The crew were unaware that the aircraft had banked to the right.
The aircraft entered a heavy turn to the right, spiralling down without any possible recovery and crashed at high-speed.

events.text: The aircraft instantaneously banked to the left shortly after taking off due to mechanical failure.
The crew conducted a fuel transfer from the left tank to the right tank, creating imbalance towards the right.
The aircraft entered a heavy turn to the right, spiralling down.
The aircraft crashed into Bo-Dzhausa Mountain with a vertical speed of about 300 m/s and a pitch angle of about 70 degrees.

title: ValuJet 592
summary: ValuJet Flight 592 crashed into the Florida Everglades about ten minutes after departing Miami on May 11, 1996. A fire developed in the cargo compartment caused by 144 expired chemical oxygen generators placed in cargo compartment boxes marked COMAT by maintenance contractor SabreTech. The fire caused progressive failure of the DC-9's electrical and flight control systems. All 110 people on board were killed, making it the deadliest aviation accident in Florida history.
probable_cause: Just before takeoff, 144 expired chemical oxygen generators were placed in the cargo compartment by ValuJet's maintenance contractor SabreTech, which violated Federal Aviation Administration regulations. The fire in the cargo compartment caused progressive failure of electrical and flight control systems leading to loss of control and crash.

factors.evidence: A fire developed in the cargo compartment caused by mislabeled and improperly stored chemical oxygen generators.
A flight attendant informed the crew of a fire in the passenger cabin.
144 expired chemical oxygen generators were placed in the cargo compartment in five boxes marked COMAT by maintenance contractor SabreTech.
The flight data recorder indicated progressive failure of the DC-9's electrical and flight control systems.

events.text: At 2:04 p.m. EDT, the DC-9 departed from Runway 9L and began a normal climb
At 2:10 p.m., passengers began to smell smoke and pilots heard a loud bang in their headsets
The sag in electrical power was determined to be the result of an explosion of a tire in the cargo hold
Kubeck and Hazen immediately asked air traffic control to return to Miami
Flight 592 disappeared from radar and crashed into the Everglades at a speed in excess of 507 mph

title: SilkAir 185
summary: SilkAir Flight 185 departed Jakarta at 15:37 local time for an 80-minute flight to Singapore. At 16:05, the cockpit voice recorder ceased recording after Captain Tsu stated he was leaving the cockpit to fetch water. The flight data recorder also stopped recording at 16:11. Flight 185 remained level at FL350 until it started a rapid and nearly vertical dive around 16:12. Parts of the aircraft separated from the fuselage due to high forces from the nearly supersonic dive, and the aircraft hit the Musi River, killing all 104 people on board.
probable_cause: The NTSC concluded that the evidence was insufficient to determine a cause. The NTSB concluded that the crash was the result of deliberate flight-control inputs, most likely by the captain. Investigators found that flight inputs had moved the horizontal stabilizer from level flight to a full nose-down descent.

factors.evidence: Investigators found that flight inputs from one of the pilots had moved the stabilizer from level flight to a full nose-down descent.
It is likely that Captain Tsu pulled out the CVR circuit breaker while exiting the cockpit.
The FDR stopped recording at 16:11, and if Captain Tsu was responsible for the crash, he must have devised some excuse to persuade the first officer to leave the flight deck.
The aircraft started a rapid and nearly vertical dive, and parts of the aircraft separated from the fuselage due to high forces from the nearly supersonic dive.

events.text: The Boeing 737 departed Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport's runway 25R for an 80-minute flight to Singapore's Changi Airport.
The cockpit voice recorder ceased recording after Captain Tsu stated he was leaving the cockpit to fetch water.
The flight data recorder stopped recording.
The aircraft started a rapid and nearly vertical dive around 16:12.
The aircraft hit the Musi River near Palembang, Sumatra, and was travelling faster than the speed of sound.

title: Flash Airlines 604
summary: The Boeing 737-300 crashed into the Red Sea three minutes after takeoff from Sharm El Sheikh. After takeoff, the autopilot abruptly disconnected and the aircraft entered a steep right bank that increased to 111 degrees where it stalled. The NTSB and BEA concluded the pilot suffered spatial disorientation and the copilot was unwilling to challenge the more experienced captain.
probable_cause: The NTSB and BEA concluded that the pilot suffered spatial disorientation and the copilot was unwilling to challenge his more experienced superior. Egyptian authorities disagreed, instead blaming mechanical issues.

factors.evidence: The autopilot abruptly disconnected at which point the aircraft entered a right bank of 40 degrees.
The NTSB and BEA concluded that the pilot suffered spatial disorientation.
The copilot was unwilling to challenge his more experienced superior.
Both officers were insufficiently trained.
The aircraft entered a stall and crashed into the Red Sea at 04:45 EGY, just three minutes after takeoff.

events.text: The aircraft departed and made a left turn to intercept the airport's VOR system, and the autopilot was then engaged; Captain Khedr made an unintelligible exclamation and the autopilot abruptly disconnected.
The aircraft entered a right bank of 40 degrees and the bank angle increased further.
First Officer al-Shaafei called out 'overbank,' indicating that the aircraft's bank was becoming dangerous.
The aircraft entered a stall and crashed into the Red Sea at 04:45 EGY, just three minutes after takeoff.

title: Mandala Airlines 091
summary: Mandala Airlines Flight 091 crashed into a residential area seconds after taking off from Polonia International Airport on September 5, 2005. The flight crew did not configure the aircraft properly for takeoff with flaps and slats retracted. The retracted flaps and slats resulted in the aircraft being unable to fly due to insufficient lift. The aircraft stalled and veered left and right, with the tail impacting the runway before crashing into the road. Of 117 on board, only 17 survived and 49 civilians on the ground were killed.
probable_cause: The crash was caused by the actions of the flight crew in that they did not configure the aircraft properly for takeoff. The retracted flaps and slats resulted in the aircraft being unable to fly due to insufficient lift. The takeoff warning was not heard and pilots may not have been aware of their erroneous actions.

factors.evidence: The flight crew did not configure the aircraft properly for takeoff with flaps and slats retracted.
The aircraft briefly took off then stalled and veered left and right.
The aircraft takeoff warning was not heard and investigators stated it was possible the pilots did not receive a warning about improper configuration.
The aircraft stalled and the tail impacted the runway before crashing into the road.

events.text: Aircraft pushed back at 09:52 a.m. and start-up clearance was given immediately
It then taxied out onto Runway 23 and was cleared to take off at 10:03 a.m.
Flight crews then added thrust and the aircraft began rolling on the runway
Aircraft took longer than usual to take off from airport even though aircraft was already in nose up position
Aircraft briefly took off then veered to the left and to the right and stalled and then the tail impacted the runway
Aircraft then struck several approach lights located at end of runway before crossing small river

title: Armavia 967

agencies.name: Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety

summary: Armavia Flight 967 was attempting a go-around following its first approach to Sochi airport at night with weather below landing minimums. While performing the climb with the autopilot disengaged, the captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness. The insufficient pitch-control inputs led to failure to recover the aircraft and it crashed into the sea. All 113 aboard were killed.
probable_cause: The captain, being in a psychoemotional stress condition, made nose-down control inputs due to the loss of pitch and roll awareness while performing the climb after an aborted approach. The first officer's lack of monitoring the aircraft's pitch attitude and altitude, and no proper reaction to GPWS warnings, contributed to the crash.

factors.evidence: The captain lost pitch and roll awareness while performing the climb with autopilot disengaged.
The captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness.
The first officer failed to monitor the aircraft's pitch attitude, altitude, and vertical speed.
There was no proper reaction by the crew to GPWS warnings.
The aircraft crashed into the sea while conducting a climbing maneuver after an aborted approach.

events.text: The airplane took off from Zvartnots airport at 20:47 with 113 occupants on board
Crew decided to continue the flight to Sochi airport at 21:31
Crew reported gear down and ready for landing, then performed go-around after overshooting the runway extended centreline
During climb with autopilot disengaged, captain made nose-down control inputs due to loss of pitch and roll awareness
GPWS warnings sounded during the climb
The aircraft crashed into the sea after the crew's insufficient pitch-control inputs led to failure to recover

title: Aeroflot 821
summary: Aeroflot Flight 821 crashed on approach to Perm International Airport at 05:10 local time when both pilots lost spatial orientation. The primary cause was that both pilots had lost spatial orientation due to their inexperience with the Western type of attitude indicator on the aircraft. The plane banked left, overturned and went into a rapid descent. Poor crew resource management and insufficient training for using the Western type of attitude indicators contributed to the accident.
probable_cause: The immediate cause of the accident was the loss of spatial orientation by the crew, chiefly by the captain, who was piloting the aircraft during the landing phase. The plane banked left, overturned and went into a rapid descent. Poor crew resource management and insufficient training contributed to the accident.

factors.evidence: Both pilots had lost spatial orientation due to their inexperience with the Western type of attitude indicator on the aircraft.
Insufficient training for using the Western type of attitude indicators contributed to the accident.
Poor crew resource management contributed to the accident.
The captain's flight record as a captain was 452 hours.
The plane banked left, overturned and went into a rapid descent.

events.text: Aeroflot Flight 821 approaching Perm at night while flying in clouds with autopilot switched off
After going around, the aircraft turned eastward instead of westward
Radio contact with the plane was lost as the aircraft crashed on the outskirts of Perm
The airplane fell into a ravine near the city limits completely destroyed and on fire
